item.title: Comparison of melanin subtypes using pump-probe microscopy
item.description: arXiv:2610.40969v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pump-probe microscopy (PPM) is used to probe excited state dynamics of endogenous chromophores to generate contrast that is unavailable in traditional forms of microscopy. Here we apply PPM to characterize melanin, a pigment central to photoprotection, skin and eye pigmentation, and melanoma pathogenesis. item.description: arXiv:2610.40904v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sender authentication is an important requirement for secure quantum communication networks. item.description: arXiv:2610.41261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cryogenic crystalline silicon is a promising optical material for next generation gravitational-wave detectors due to its low mechanical loss (a driver of thermal noise), high thermal conductivity and zero coefficient of thermal expansion at 123 K. item.description: arXiv:2610.41503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Waveguide-based Raman spectroscopy offers a route toward compact and integrated photonic sensors. item.description: arXiv:2610.42003v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cavity enhancement of emission from a point source typically relies on structures that preserve its cylindrical symmetry, such as circular Bragg gratings. item.title: Experiment supports theoretical foundation for potentially more error-resistant quantum computing
item.description: One approach to making information storage in quantum computing less prone to errors is known as topological quantum computing. It relies on special quantum states that are expected to be more resistant to local disturbances.

item.title: Ultrathin kagome material opens a route to study unusual quantum states
item.description: How atoms are arranged inside materials can influence the behavior of electrons and the resulting electronic states. Kagome lattices, repeating arrangements of atoms forming triangles that share corners (with hexagonal spaces between them), have been linked with the emergence of unusual electronic states.

item.description: arXiv:2610.40979v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical spin-orbit interactions (SOI), demonstrated experimentally in optical cavities, enable the polarization degrees of freedom of light to be described and controlled as an effective pseudospin, providing a foundation for spintronic-like control of light and the development of next-generation optical technologies. item.description: arXiv:2610.41315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We theoretically find that a cylindrical microresonator with nanoscale radius variation can be a source of coherent microcombs with two repetition rates, independently controlled by the device geometry. item.description: arXiv:2610.41370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-Hermitian spectral topology has transformed our understanding of bulk--boundary correspondence in open systems, yet its exploration has largely remained within the Markovian regime of instantaneous coupling. item.description: arXiv:2610.41392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The reconfigurable generation of complex structured terahertz (THz) fields, and vector beams in particular, remains a significant challenge. item.description: arXiv:2610.41531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Image priors can dramatically improve phase retrieval reconstruction, but their effectiveness strongly varies between imaging modalities. item.description: arXiv:2610.41917v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Real-world deployment of quantum technologies requires systems in low SWaP-C packages. item.description: arXiv:2610.42098v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The optical Kerr effect, whereby the refractive index of a material changes with light intensity, underpins nonlinear photonics and emerging mid-infrared technologies. item.description: arXiv:2610.40952v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a characterization of the sensitivity of broadband electric field measurements in the Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands using AC stark shifting of Rydberg states. item.description: arXiv:2610.41061v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The inverse Faraday effect (IFE) (the generation of an effective magnetic field in a material upon irradiation with circularly polarized light) offers a pathway to ultrafast, non-thermal control of spin dynamics. item.title: Spectral Information Content of Diffraction-Limited Images
item.description: arXiv:2610.41092v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: High-resolution optical imaging is fundamentally limited by diffraction, which imprints wavelength-dependent structure onto the point spread function (PSF) of the optical system. This intrinsic chromaticity implies that in addition to spatial structure, images encode spectral information. item.description: arXiv:2610.41198v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this work, we investigate the practical feasibility of achieving a quantum advantage, in the context of inter-satellite quantum communication, of satellite position estimation. item.description: arXiv:2610.41270v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Optical springs tailor the response of precision sensors. Parametric amplification of the signal field stiffens the spring, extending the precision to higher frequencies. A Michelson interferometer operated at a dark fringe is the most direct way to separate the signal from the carrier for amplification. item.title: Single molecules could provide the building blocks for future quantum networks
item.description: Quantum computers rely on qubits as their units of information. To connect them into a larger network across long distances, they need to transmit quantum information using light.

item.title: Theoretical method uses light to locate anyons, potential quantum computing building blocks
item.description: Theoretical physicists at Emory University have discovered a way to use light to detect the "spectral fingerprints" of anyons—exotic quasiparticles that emerge from the collective behavior of many electrons. Their findings are published in Physical Review Letters. The work offers a new tool for the study of anyons, which hold potential as fundamental building blocks for quantum computing.
